feature.summary: Explains and handles runs that did not happen on time or failed. The Cloud sweep decides a run is missed when it starts more than two sweep intervals late and then runs it late once or skips it, as the owner chose, and the run history says so. Failed or timed-out runs retry with doubling waits. Holding runs for usage resets and repairing expired connectors are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Records why an occurrence ran late or was skipped, applies the owner's 'If A Run Is Missed' choice, retries failed or timed-out runs a chosen number of times with doubling waits, and writes an audit event for missed runs. On Electron Desktop, Local routines have their own missed-run choice and a 2 minute grace.
purpose.why_it_exists: The Cloud sweep runs about every 15 minutes, machines sleep, and models fail. People need to see what happened to an occurrence instead of guessing (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/063-routines-schedules-and-triggers.md, S63.33 to S63.35).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners reading run history on any app; operators reading audit events.
problems_solved: A routine fired hours late: the history says 'Ran late: scheduled for X, started Y later.'
A stale occurrence should not run: choose skip and see 'Skipped the run scheduled for X'.
A flaky run: retries try again before the routine moves on.
A skipped run must not use up the run limit: the slot is given back.
use_cases: Morning digest that is pointless after noon: set 'Skip it and wait for the next occurrence'.
Billing report that must still happen: keep 'Run it once, late'.
Flaky external site: Retries After A Failed Run 3, first retry after 5 minutes.
Check why a routine did not run overnight in the run history.

'Retries After A Failed Run' (0 to 5) and 'First Retry After (Minutes)' (1 to 1440); helper: 'A failed or timed-out run is tried again after this wait, doubling each time, before the schedule moves on to its next occurrence.' (ScheduleForm.tsx:592-640).

journey: Choose the missed-run policy and retry settings in the routine form and save.
The sweep claims a due occurrence. If it is more than the grace period late, the missed-run rule applies.
Run it once, late: the run goes ahead and its result carries the missed-run details; the history says 'Ran late: scheduled for <when>, started <how late> later.'

Skip: the run is recorded as cancelled with skipped, the run slot is returned, and the history says 'Skipped the run scheduled for <when>: it was missed by <how late>, and this schedule skips missed runs.'
If a run fails or times out and retries remain, the routine is scheduled again after the wait (doubling) for the same occurrence.
Open run history to read notes, errors and output.
feedback_and_outputs: Notes from describeScheduleRunTiming: 'Ran late...' and 'Skipped the run scheduled for...' and, for condition watches, 'Skipped: the condition was not met. <detail>' (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:740-765).
Run error text for a skip: 'Skipped the occurrence scheduled for <time>: it was missed by more than the grace period' (schedule-service.ts:2264).
Audit event type schedule_missed_execution with outcome success for run late and failure for skip (schedule-service.ts:2120-2138).
Failed or timed-out status badge and error text on the run (ScheduleRunHistory.tsx:87, :172-176).
settings: retryMaxAttempts 0 to 5, default 0; retryBackoffSeconds 60 to 86,400, default 300 (schedule-service.ts:86-89, :741-757).
AGI_DB_LOW_POWER environment setting raises the grace to two hours and limits sweeps (apps/web/lib/server/cron-low-power.ts:6-21; schedule-service.ts:81-85).

working: Detection: late by more than missedExecutionGraceMs counts as missed; applies only to scheduled, first attempts (schedule-service.ts:2102-2118). Grace is twice the 15 minute sweep interval (30 minutes) or twice an hour in low-power mode (packages/platform/utils/src/scheduling/schedule-time.ts:259; schedule-service.ts:81-85).

Policy: skip finalizes the run as cancelled with {missedExecution, skipped:true}, returns the run slot; run_once continues and stores the missed details in the result; both write an audit event (schedule-service.ts:2256-2268, :2120-2138, :2156-2166).
A run that resumes after approval keeps its missed-run details (schedule-service.ts:2220, :2039).

Retries: failed or timeout, scheduled triggers only, while retriesSpent is below retryMaxAttempts, no cap reached and the expiry not passed; delay is backoff doubled per retry, exponent capped at 10, capped at one day; a retry claims under its own key and does not spend a run (schedule-service.ts:1643-1647, :1713-1735; :1381-1382).
Shared note text via describeScheduleRunTiming, used by Web, Tauri desktop, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome (see user_experience).
Condition-not-met runs are also recorded as skipped and give the run slot back (schedule-service.ts:2269-2277).

Electron Local routines: missed beyond 120 seconds with policy skip records a run in state 'skipped'; run_once starts it; a computer sleep marks the interrupted claim and never replays it (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/localRoutineEngine.ts:145, :511-537; test title apps/desktop/electron/__tests__/localRoutineEngine.test.ts:587).
Expired worker leases are recovered by the sweep so a run does not stay 'running' for ever (schedule-service.ts:2360-2400; exact recovery steps not read).

A routine whose owner left the workspace is not claimed and only a server warning is logged; the owner sees nothing on the routine (schedule-service.ts:1317-1335).

established.statement: S63.33: when an occurrence is missed or skipped, the run history says so and why. Done on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code; the brief lists Chrome as none.
S63.34: a run that hits the usage allowance is held and runs automatically after the allowance resets. Missing on every app.
S63.35: when a connector a routine depends on expires, the user is told on the routine and led to reconnect. Missing on every app.
A run is missed when it starts more than twice the sweep interval late; run_once runs it late, skip records it and gives the run slot back; both write an audit event.
Failed or timed-out scheduled runs retry with doubling wait up to the chosen count (0 to 5).
The note text comes from describeScheduleRunTiming in the shared contracts.
Mobile v1 only needs the pieces required for Cloud sign-in and future dispatch; Desktop and CLI carry deeper automation later.

acceptance_criteria: A scheduled occurrence started more than 30 minutes after its due time (normal mode) is treated as missed; one started within 30 minutes is not.
With 'Run it once, late' the run executes and its history note reads 'Ran late: scheduled for <time>, started <duration> later.'
With 'Skip it...' no model call happens, the run shows as skipped with the skip note, and the routine's run counter is not increased by that occurrence.
Both policies create a schedule_missed_execution audit event.
With Retries After A Failed Run 2 and first retry 5 minutes, a failed run is tried again after 5 minutes, then 10 minutes, then the routine moves on; a manual run is not retried.
A retry does not reduce the Maximum Runs allowance.
Run history on Web, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome shows the same note text for the same run.
A Local routine on Electron with skip and a due time more than 2 minutes old shows state 'skipped'.
inferred: The Chrome run list should show missed notes because it calls the shared function, but no test title for it was found [inferred] (schedulesSection.ts:1077).

A usage-allowance refusal currently surfaces as a failed run (which retries if configured) because the reservation call is not guarded in runClaimedSchedule [inferred] (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:1056; schedule-service.ts:2309-2335).
The two-sweep grace means a routine only appears missed after about 30 minutes, which is roughly two missed cron ticks [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Hold a run that hits the allowance, show 'Waiting for your allowance to reset', and run it after the reset time.
[proposed] When a connector token has expired, mark the run and the routine with a repair link to the connector screen.
[proposed] Show the skip note on CLI and Mobile with the same wording as Web.
[proposed] Tell the owner on the routine when a workspace departure stops it from running.

steps.what_happens: Vercel cron calls /api/cron/run-schedules every 15 minutes; in low-power mode it returns early after minute 15 of the hour.

The sweep cancels expired approvals, recovers expired leases, then claims due routines (enabled, active, next run due, not past expiry, under run limit unless retrying, owner allowed to run unattended and active in the workspace). The claim inserts a run row with an idempotency key built from the due time and retry number.
For each claim, the cap check runs; then missed detection compares now with the due time; skip policy finalizes the run as cancelled, run_once continues.
The executor runs the routine (model call to the provider); on error the status becomes failed, on timeout timeout, on outside cancel cancelled.

finalizeScheduleRun writes the run result and decides the next time: retry with doubling delay, or next occurrence, or completed/expired, or pause at cap; failed and timed-out runs queue a notification, cancelled ones do not.
Clients list runs; the shared function turns the stored missedExecution and skipped fields into the note text.
Electron Local routines: the on-device engine ticks every second and applies its own missed rule with a 120 second grace.

data.synced: Returned with each run through the API

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The missed and retry logic does not depend on a model. A retried or late run goes through normal route selection; retries of a failed provider call use the same managed path. Nothing in this feature switches model or provider on failure (no such code found in the retry branch).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account to read history; the sweep acts for the routine owner and skips owners whose account state forbids unattended work or who left the workspace (schedule-service.ts:1366-1368, :1317-1335).
access_and_usage.permissions: Owner reads their own runs. Workspace admin visibility of skipped work: only a server log line (schedule-service.ts:1328-1335).
access_and_usage.subscription: A run for an account without managed compute access is cancelled by the executor with a reason (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:889-915). A usage-allowance hold: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Retries 0 to 5; backoff 60 to 86,400 seconds, default 300; retry delay doubles with the exponent capped at 10 (schedule-service.ts:86-89, :1643-1647). Retries do not spend a run (schedule-service.ts:1381-1382). Sweep batch limits are in the cron route (not detailed).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: None found in the code for missed or retry rules.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None found in the code for these rules.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Cloud sweep, retries and the missed policy do not apply in Local mode. Electron Local routines have a skip-or-run missed rule with a 2 minute grace, run only while the Desktop app is open, and have no retry code (localRoutineEngine.ts:145, :511-537; LocalRoutinesSection.tsx:218-222; the text 'Runs while the Desktop app is open').

scenarios.name: Run it once, late

scenarios.name: Skip

missing_facts: A reached credit cap stops retries. When a retry would otherwise fire, the cap pauses the routine, via isCreditCapReached in the retry predicate and the pauseForCreditCap path (schedule-service.ts:1643-1647, :2130-2250). The page names the cap only in passing.
A run resumed after approval skips both missed detection and the condition check (`if (!options.resume)`, schedule-service.ts:2256-2257). The page notes only that the missed details are kept.

The skip error text is 'Skipped the occurrence scheduled for ...' but a condition-watch skip is stored as status 'cancelled' with the error 'Condition not met: ...' (schedule-service.ts:2269-2277). The page covers this only through the note text.
